findings.description: Subcommand write path is wrong. The plan says subcommands 'load current snapshot → apply mutation → call writeSidecar()'. But writeSidecar() in scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs expects Ralph sidecar state with top-level byTaskId/generatedAt/generatedFromCommit/unmatched, not the plans/overview-snapshot.json shape (tasks[], schemaVersion, ralph subfield on each task). Implementing literally will wipe Ralph data from emitted artifacts.
findings.resolution: Updated Story 7 and matching acceptance criteria to use the Ralph sidecar write path and clarify that writeSidecar regenerates the derived snapshot.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify that subcommands load config.outputs.sidecarJson (plans/overview-ralph-state.json) — the Ralph sidecar — and mutate byTaskId there before calling writeSidecar(). The snapshot is regenerated by writeSidecar() downstream. Add an explicit example in Story 7.

findings.description: Partial-entry race: when /work-on --via-crew times out before manifest sessionId/transcriptPath are populated, it records a partial explicit entry with no sessionId. The merge rule dedupes 'by sessionId', so a later heuristic discovery of the same member will not merge with the partial entry — it creates a duplicate.
findings.resolution: Amended the plan to use fallback (crewName, memberName) identity for partial crew-session entries, upgrade them in place when heuristic data later supplies sessionId/transcriptPath, and require test coverage for that race.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a fallback identity key (crewName, memberName) when sessionId is absent. Define an upgrade rule: heuristic discovery that finds a partial explicit entry (matched by (crewName, memberName)) upgrades it in place by filling in sessionId, transcriptPath, startedAt. Cover with a test (US-011 conflict resolution should include the partial-entry case).

findings.sectionRef: Approach > Architecture (Watcher integration) / Files to Modify
findings.description: parseWatchedPath() in scripts/lib/watch-ralph-state.mjs (lines ~273-304) has a hardcoded rootEntries array with three items (job, group, brainstorm). The plan says it will recognize a new 'crews' kind, but doesn't specify the code structure. Additionally, the flush handler currently maps every pending change to deriveAffectedTaskUpdate({ repoRoot, config, kind, slug, ... }). For kind='crews' with no slug, deriveAffectedTaskUpdate's behavior is undefined.
findings.resolution: Amended the watcher plan to detect .crews roots before Ralph root parsing and route crew events through a dedicated rescanCrewSessionsAndWrite helper instead of deriveAffectedTaskUpdate.
findings.suggestedFix: In Story 6, specify: (a) parseWatchedPath() detects .crews/crews/ and .crews/sessions-configs/ paths BEFORE the Ralph rootEntries loop and returns {kind: 'crews'} with no slug; (b) the flush handler branches on kind==='crews' and invokes a new dedicated helper rescanCrewSessionsAndWrite(currentState, config, repoRoot, overviewData) instead of deriveAffectedTaskUpdate. This helper re-runs discoverCrewSessions, merges results into currentState.byTaskId[*].crewSessions (preserving _isExplicit entries), and calls writeSidecar() with no Ralph re-derivation.

findings.description: discoverCrewSessions matches members to taskId, but crewSessions is keyed by RalphStage. Plan does not specify how to derive the stage for a heuristic discovery. Without an explicit rule, all sessions could land in the same stage bucket or fail to render.
findings.resolution: Amended the plan to derive heuristic crew-session stage from ralphState.byTaskId[taskId].stage, preserve recorded stage buckets across later task advancement, and require tests for the implementing-to-reviewing case.
findings.suggestedFix: Add explicit rule: 'When discoverCrewSessions matches a member to taskId, it reads the stage from ralphState.byTaskId[taskId].stage at discovery time and assigns the session to that stage bucket. If the task later advances to a different stage, existing entries remain under their recorded stage and are NOT migrated.' Add a test confirming an entry recorded under stage='implementing' stays there after the task advances to 'reviewing'.

findings.description: .ralph/overview-config.schema.json has additionalProperties: false at the top level. Adding crewsRoot to default-config.mjs without also adding it to the schema will cause schema-validated configs to be rejected.
findings.resolution: Updated Story 2 and its acceptance criterion to require a top-level schema properties.crewsRoot string entry and validation of configs that set crewsRoot.
findings.suggestedFix: Story 2 must explicitly call out adding {"crewsRoot": {"type": "string"}} to the schema properties block, alongside dataFile/ralphRoot/lockFile/watcher. Acceptance criterion: schema validation of a config that sets crewsRoot succeeds.

findings.description: scripts/lib/resolve-config.mjs's resolveConfigPaths() destructures known fields and returns them; unknown fields are dropped. If Story 2 adds crewsRoot only to default-config.mjs but not to resolve-config.mjs's destructuring and return statement, the field will be silently dropped and watch roots won't include .crews/.
findings.resolution: Story 2 now explicitly requires resolve-config.mjs to destructure and return crewsRoot, plus a resolver test that verifies crewsRoot overrides resolve to absolute paths.
findings.suggestedFix: Story 2 must explicitly specify: extract crewsRoot from the input config and add `crewsRoot: resolvePath(repoRoot, config.crewsRoot)` to the returned object. Add a test: loading a config with crewsRoot set produces an absolute resolved path.

findings.description: scripts/lib/default-config.d.mts defines RalphOverviewConfig interface; downstream TS callers won't see crewsRoot if it's not declared. The plan mentions '+2 lines' but doesn't show the structure.
findings.resolution: Amended Story 2 to explicitly require adding top-level crewsRoot: string to the RalphOverviewConfig interface in scripts/lib/default-config.d.mts.
findings.suggestedFix: Story 2 explicitly adds crewsRoot: string to the RalphOverviewConfig interface. Required (not optional) because default-config.mjs provides a default value.

findings.description: discoverCrewSessions integration with parse-spawn-launcher is underspecified. Plan creates parse-spawn-launcher.mjs but says discoverCrewSessions 'walks manifests' — it doesn't say how/when launchers are scanned, indexed by (crewName, memberName), or how multiple launchers per member are disambiguated.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify: discoverCrewSessions builds an index of .crews/spawn-launchers/*.ps1 keyed by (crewName, memberName), parsing each via parseSpawnLauncher. When multiple launchers exist for a member (re-spawns), pick the one whose filename timestamp is latest. The medium-signal match (initial-prompt contains taskId) reads from this index. Document this in the Heuristic matching contract section.

findings.description: path.relative(repoRoot, manifestCwd) returns '' (empty string) when manifestCwd === repoRoot. The plan says 'verify the result is non-empty, non-absolute, and not prefixed with ..' — that rejects the happy path (members spawned with --cwd at the repo root). Real manifests have cwd: 'D:\\harness-efforts\\codexu' which equals repoRoot exactly.
findings.resolution: Updated the cwd-filter contract and test expectations so manifests at the repo root are accepted while prefix-attack paths remain rejected.
findings.suggestedFix: Correct the cwd-filter contract: accept the manifest when path.relative(repoRoot, manifestCwd) is either '' OR a relative path that doesn't start with '..' and isn't absolute. Add explicit test for cwd === repoRoot case.

findings.description: Default crewsRoot = path.join(repoRoot, '.crews') resolves to the worktree's .crews/ when code runs inside .ralph/jobs/ralph-pipeline-08-crews/worktree/. The plan says .crews/ MUST resolve from the main repo root, but the default rule violates that.
findings.resolution: Updated the plan so default crewsRoot resolves to the main repo .crews when repoRoot is a linked worktree, with resolver and acceptance-test requirements.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify a main-root resolution rule: when repoRoot is a worktree (detect via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` differing from `git rev-parse --git-dir`), resolve crewsRoot to the COMMON repo root (path.join(common, '..', '.crews')), not the worktree's own .crews. The watcher / subcommands / cross-walk all share this resolution. Add a test covering worktree mode.

findings.description: tools/overview-viewer/CLAUDE.md requires an Ajv regression test in scripts/lib/emit-snapshot-schema.test.mjs whenever fields are added to RalphPipelineState. The plan updates emit-snapshot-schema.mjs but doesn't list the test update. The existing permissive 'future-plan-extension' allowance is not enough to prove the explicit crewSessions contract.
findings.resolution: Added explicit cascade-audit requirements to update emit-snapshot-schema.test.mjs with positive crewSessions validation and malformed CrewSessionRef rejection coverage.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an explicit story (or add to US-001) updating scripts/lib/emit-snapshot-schema.test.mjs with a positive case: a snapshot containing crewSessions validates; a snapshot with a malformed CrewSessionRef (e.g., missing required memberName) fails validation.

findings.description: Plan says 'all mailbox/outbox files' must be added to ignored patterns but doesn't define the patterns. The .crews/ structure (per the seed plan) has mailbox.json and outbox.jsonl INSIDE each member/lead directory at .crews/crews/<crew>/members/<name>/mailbox.json — not at .crews/mailboxes/**.
findings.resolution: Amended the draft plan tmp file to specify the exact .crews mailbox, outbox, and inbox-history chokidar ignore patterns in the watcher/config sections.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify explicit chokidar patterns: '.crews/crews/*/members/*/mailbox.json', '.crews/crews/*/members/*/outbox.jsonl', '.crews/crews/*/leads/*/mailbox.json', '.crews/crews/*/leads/*/outbox.jsonl', '.crews/crews/*/inbox-history.jsonl'. The watcher already excludes .crews/logs/** and .crews/spawn-launchers/**; add these alongside.

findings.description: Subcommands should validate stage and outcome inputs. Otherwise --update-crew-session <id> <stage> can write invalid stage keys that TaskCommand.tsx will never render, and --finalize-crew-session can set outcomes outside the documented enum.
findings.suggestedFix: Validate stage against the canonical RalphStage union (imported/duplicated from types.ts; e.g., 'planning'|'implementing'|'reviewing'|...). Validate outcome against ('completed'|'handed-off'|'stopped'|'failed'). Exit non-zero with a clear error on invalid input. Add tests.

findings.description: /work-on --via-crew spawns the member BEFORE checking lock availability. If pnpm overview is running, the spawn-member side effect runs, but the subsequent --update-crew-session call fails on lock contention — leaving an unrecorded or only-heuristically-discovered member.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a lock preflight step in /work-on --via-crew: before calling spawn-member, check whether the watcher lock is held by another process (read lockfile JSON; check pid liveness). If held, abort with a clear message instructing the user to stop pnpm overview first. Add this as a test case.

findings.description: Plan says transcript link is built by 'convert Windows backslashes to forward slashes'. That's insufficient for safe file:// URLs — drive letters, spaces, and # characters can break links. Both Codex and Copilot flagged this.
findings.suggestedFix: Use Node's pathToFileURL(transcriptPath).href server-side OR mirror its escaping rules client-side (component runs in browser; manually URL-encode drive letter, path segments, and # / spaces). Acceptance criterion: a transcriptPath like 'C:\\Users\\evmitran\\.claude\\projects\\with#hash\\session.jsonl' produces a valid clickable file:// URL.

findings.description: CrewSessionRef field shape is not fully enumerated. The seed plan's interface listed crewName/memberName/sessionId/transcriptPath/startedAt/endedAt?/outcome?/summary?, but the draft plan also adds _isExplicit and introduces a partial-entry concept where sessionId/transcriptPath may be absent. The AC should explicitly enumerate required vs optional fields.
findings.suggestedFix: Spell out the final interface in the plan: required (crewName, memberName, startedAt); optional (sessionId, transcriptPath, endedAt, outcome, summary, _isExplicit, cwd). Note the optional-ness reflects manifest-race and stale-entry states.

findings.description: AC says 'typecheck across packages' but root package.json has no root 'typecheck' script. Test commands are not specific.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace 'typecheck across packages' with explicit commands: 'pnpm test' (root vitest), 'pnpm --filter @codexu/overview-viewer test' (split vitest projects), 'pnpm --filter @codexu/overview-viewer typecheck', 'pnpm -r --if-present typecheck'.

findings.description: Plan says 'the explicit-vs-heuristic merge runs WITHIN a tick using the prior snapshot's crewSessions ... as the authoritative explicit set', but doesn't specify HOW the prior snapshot is loaded and threaded into assembleStateFromBundles(). The current function signature is {bundles, repoRoot, config, generatedFromCommit} with no prior-state parameter.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify: walkRalphState reads config.outputs.sidecarJson if it exists, extracts crewSessions per task, and threads them as priorCrewSessions into assembleStateFromBundles. assembleStateFromBundles passes priorCrewSessions to discoverCrewSessions, which uses them as the authoritative explicit set during merge. Add a test covering tick N+1 preserves explicit entries from tick N.

findings.description: Plan doesn't specify the full pseudocode for replacing the Plan-06 placeholder error in SKILL.md, nor what /work-on --via-crew returns to the user (silent ref-write or confirmation message with session ID).
findings.suggestedFix: In Story 8, add pseudocode showing each step of the flow (preflight lock, derive command via derive-next-command-cli.mjs, generate member name, spawn via CLI mirror, poll manifest 10s/500ms, write ref via --update-crew-session, print confirmation including member name + session ID or 'pending' status). The output is a short summary message to the lead, not the full transcript.

findings.description: Watcher 'crews event triggers full crew-rescan without Ralph re-derive' should be a dedicated helper (e.g., mergeCrewSessionsIntoState / rescanCrewSessionsAndWrite), not forced through deriveAffectedTaskUpdate with a synthetic kind. Both Claude and Copilot flagged this.
findings.suggestedFix: Story 6 introduces rescanCrewSessionsAndWrite({currentState, config, repoRoot, overviewData, priorCrewSessions}) in sync-core.mjs. The flush handler branches on kind==='crews' and calls this helper directly instead of deriveAffectedTaskUpdate. The helper re-runs discoverCrewSessions, merges into currentState.byTaskId[*].crewSessions (preserving _isExplicit), and calls writeSidecar. Add a test.

findings.description: Config plumbing must also touch normalizeConfigPaths() in scripts/lib/sync-core.mjs. Direct callers/tests pass default config objects through walkRalphState/assembleStateFromBundles, and crewsRoot must be resolved consistently there too — not only in resolve-config.mjs.
findings.suggestedFix: Story 2 also updates normalizeConfigPaths() in sync-core.mjs to populate crewsRoot when callers don't provide it (mirroring how the default is resolved elsewhere). Add a test verifying that walkRalphState({repoRoot, config: {}}) results in a populated crewsRoot.

findings.description: Story 8 implies importing derive-next-command.mjs directly, but /work-on SKILL.md actually invokes the CLI helper at scripts/lib/derive-next-command-cli.mjs. Direct import would be the wrong contract.
findings.suggestedFix: Specify that /work-on --via-crew invokes `node scripts/lib/derive-next-command-cli.mjs <taskId>` (or whatever the existing CLI mirror's signature is) and parses the printed command. Do not import the JS module from within the skill.
